therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on metformin
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: HbA1c change from baseline at week 52 and week 104

results.effect_size: LS mean difference in HbA1c change at week 52: +0.22% (linagliptin vs glimepiride, 97.5% CI 0.13–0.31); at week 104: +0.20% (97.5% CI 0.09–0.30)
biomarker_changes: Linagliptin: FPG change -8.40 mg/dL at week 52 vs glimepiride -15.24 mg/dL
Linagliptin: FPG change -2.34 mg/dL at week 104 vs glimepiride -8.72 mg/dL
Linagliptin: 2hr PPG change -28.47 mg/dL at week 104 vs glimepiride -18.72 mg/dL (p=0.0918)
Linagliptin: body weight change -1.12 kg at week 52 vs glimepiride +1.38 kg
Linagliptin: body weight change -1.39 kg at week 104 vs glimepiride +1.29 kg
Linagliptin: HDL change +1 mg/dL at week 104 vs glimepiride 0
Linagliptin: triglyceride change -11 mg/dL at week 104 vs glimepiride -7 mg/dL
Linagliptin: LDL change +1 mg/dL at week 104 vs glimepiride +3 mg/dL
safety_signals: Hypoglycaemic events up to 52 weeks: 41 patients on linagliptin vs 249 on glimepiride (p<0.0001)
Hypoglycaemic events up to 104 weeks: 58 patients on linagliptin vs 280 on glimepiride (p<0.0001)
Linagliptin associated with significantly lower hypoglycaemia risk compared to glimepiride
Glimepiride associated with weight gain; linagliptin associated with weight loss

dose_info.dose_modifications: Glimepiride dose titrated from 1 mg up to 4 mg
